input: Do I have to buy to enter the freezer giveaway?
output: No. Giveaway entry is free, no purchase is necessary, and buying does not improve your odds. If you also place a qualifying stocked-home order, the cheesecake thank-you gift is a separate order bonus.

input: What box should I start with for a family of four?
output: Start with the Family Box if you want practical weekly meals. If you want a smaller first order, choose Starter Box. If you are filling a larger freezer, Rancher Box gives more depth and flexibility.

input: Do you deliver to my ZIP?
output: Start with your ZIP code so I can check the delivery route estimate. If your area is confirmed, we show the route day and window. If it is still building, we can save your interest for the next grouped delivery.

input: What does the cheesecake offer mean?
output: The cheesecake is a limited thank-you gift for qualifying first stocked-home orders reserved within the stated window, while supplies last. It is separate from giveaway entry and does not affect giveaway odds.

input: How do I continue my box later?
output: Use Continue My Box or the saved confirmation page. Your plan is saved on this device, and the concierge opens only when you choose to continue or edit details.

input: Can I clear my saved details?
output: Yes. On the confirmation page, choose Clear Saved Info to remove the saved ZIP, plan details, and contact summary from this device.

input: What was saved after I checked my route?
output: The confirmation page can show saved ZIP, plan interest, budget, route estimate, delivery timing, and masked contact details. It keeps the next step clear without reopening the popup automatically.

input: What do I need to turn in at the end of the day?
output: Turn in completed stops, missed stops, reschedules, payments, customer notes, fulfillment status, substitutions, restock issues, fuel start, fuel end, miles driven, and owner follow-up needs.

input: An order was partially fulfilled because filet was short. What should I record?
output: Record the order ID, route, partial fulfillment status, filet shortage, any substitution offered, customer note, and whether owner review is needed before the next premium promise.

input: How should I report route fuel efficiency?
output: Enter starting fuel, ending fuel, and miles driven. The system scores efficiency from those values and sends the route-learning signal to owner review.

input: How do I use voice notes on the driver page?
output: Open the active stop, tap Voice Customer Note, Voice Issue, or Voice Owner Follow-Up, then speak the note. If browser speech support is unavailable, type into the same fields.

input: How do I open navigation for a stop?
output: Use the Navigate button on the active stop. It opens Google Maps with the best available search target: full address when available, otherwise customer, ZIP, route area, and Sacramento.

input: How do I open the full route map?
output: Use Open Route Map at the top of Driver Mobile. It launches Google Maps directions for the grouped route using addresses when available and ZIP/customer fallbacks when not.

input: What should the AI co-pilot do while I am driving the route?
output: The driver AI co-pilot should stay focused on the active route: next best stop, customer text drafts, issue review, route summary, turn-in prep, voice-note cleanup, and owner follow-up. It should not expose owner reports or private customer data beyond assigned stops.

input: Draft a customer arrival text for my active stop.
output: Use the active stop details to write a short, professional delivery text with the route window, box name, and a request for gate, parking, or drop-off notes. Keep it ready to copy into SMS without making promises the driver cannot control.

input: Summarize my route before turn-in.
output: Summarize delivered stops, open stops, missed or rescheduled stops, issue flags, partial fulfillment, restock blockers, payments, miles, fuel, and owner follow-up so the driver can submit a clean end-of-day turn-in.

input: What should I check before promising premium boxes?
output: Check active restock issues, premium cut availability, route capacity, driver notes, partial fulfillment history, and recent customer preferences. Do not promise premium boxes when unresolved restock blockers exist.

input: How do we keep the route model learning without external APIs?
output: Store order, route, driver update, restock, fuel, and customer preference events in the repo-owned database format. Export reviewed records as JSONL and feed them into local retrieval or local fine-tuning tools.

input: Vercel says build failed. What should I check first?
output: Check whether the target URL is a build-rate-limit page. Then verify package versions exist, use npm install --legacy-peer-deps, and build with npm run build, which currently runs next build --webpack.

input: What went wrong with TypeScript during deployment?
output: typescript@5.7.0 was pinned but does not exist as an npm release. Use typescript@5.7.3 and confirm exact versions before pinning.

input: Why does the build use webpack with Next 16?
output: Next 16 defaults to Turbopack. This app still uses webpack fallbacks for browser-only AI package behavior, so the safe production command is next build --webpack until a Turbopack-specific migration is tested.

input: How do I use the owner lead board?
output: Open Owner Command Center, use Live for real records or Sample for rehearsal, then filter by All, Hot, Wholesale, Waitlist, or Restock. Export the visible rows when you need a CSV for follow-up or review.

input: Which leads should I call first?
output: Start with restock blockers and wholesale leads, then high-value hot orders, then waitlist routes that need grouping. The board filters these so daily follow-up stays focused.

input: How do I review route demand?
output: Use the Route Demand panel on the owner lead board. It shows route day, delivery window, grouped capacity, and status so you can decide which areas need sales follow-up before dispatch.
